title: Define once, use many times
idea: MEET: the key idea - you set up a named job ONCE, then use it as often as you like. No code.

exercises.prompt: You name a job 'print_border'. How many times can you then USE that name in your plan?
options: As many times as you need
exercises.explanation: Name it once, use it as often as you like. That reuse is the main reason to name a job.

exercises.prompt: Setting up the named job and using the named job are TWO different things.
exercises.explanation: Yes. First you describe the job (set it up / define it). Then, separately, you use it. Keep them apart.

exercises.prompt: A plan says: set up 'print_border', then use print_border, print the title, use print_border again. How many times is the border job USED?
exercises.explanation: It's used twice - top and bottom. It was only SET UP once. Define once, use many: here, twice.

exercises.prompt: Order a plan that frames a title with a border, using a named job 'print_border'.
exercises.explanation: Border on top, title in the middle, border on the bottom. The one named job is used twice.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'define once, use many times' better than copying the steps each time?
options: One place to read and fix, used everywhere
exercises.explanation: With one definition, a change happens in one place and every use gets it. Copies would each need fixing.

exercises.prompt: Which situations suit 'define once, use many times'? (Pick all.)
options: A border printed at top and bottom
A greeting shown for several players
A one-off single print never repeated
A divider drawn between each section
exercises.explanation: Repeated jobs benefit most. A truly one-off job doesn't need naming - it's used only once.

exercises.prompt: Match the idea to its meaning.

pairs.right: describe the job and give it a name
make the job happen by its name
use the same named job again

exercises.explanation: Defining sets the job up; using runs it; reusing runs it again. These are the ideas you'll soon code.

exercises.prompt: If you only ever need a job once, naming it is still usually worth the effort.
exercises.explanation: Not usually. Naming shines when a job repeats or is important enough to label. A true one-off can stay inline.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: what other tool in the course lets you repeat the same steps many times?
options: a loop - repeats steps over a sequence
exercises.explanation: Loops also repeat work. A named sub-plan is for a job you call by name at chosen moments - different, both useful.
Define the job once, use its name as often as needed. That's the power a named sub-plan gives you.
